messages:
incbot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT CREATED - sev2 - region=us-west-2c symptom= elevated 5xx (504) on /v1/generate degradations (automated threshold > 5% in 5m). paging oncall oncall-jamie and sre-lead-ana. link: https://incidents.redwood.local/2419503042

oncall-jamie: acked. jumping in — gathering quick scope. taking incident commander for now.

sre-lead-ana: oncall-jamie thanks. initial metrics: 5xx spike localized to two ELB target groups for model-serving pool; error type is 504 gateway_timeout. backend instance health checks mostly healthy but connection resets visible.

oncall-jamie: running curl against ELB from jumpbox — getting consistent 504s for ~30% of requests. not all instances fail. hitting i-0a12... & i-0b34... showing latency.

eng-runtime-rahul: past similar issues have been EBS/io stalls + kernel conn reset cascades when the process blocks on disk io. can you capture iostat & dmesg from affected hosts? runbook ebs-io-stall -> https://runbooks.redwood.local/ebs-io-stalls

ops-kelly: running commands now.

ops-kelly: ```
ssh ec2-user@i-0a12abcd
sudo iostat -x 1 3
# results:
Device            r/s     w/s   rkB/s   wkB/s  avgrq-sz  avgqu-sz  await  r_await  w_await  svctm  %util
nvme1n1         0.50   120.00    4.00  1536.00     12.8    25.30   210.5    10.2   215.3   1.20  98.5
```

ops-kelly: also seeing repeated kernel backtraces referencing io_wait and nvme timeouts in dmesg.

eng-runtime-rahul: that looks like heavy write queue + very high avgqu-sz on nvme. confirms IO path issue. propose: remove these instances from ELB target group to stop user impact while we triage and coordinate with AWS.

oncall-jamie: agree. I'll drain i-0a12abcd and i-0b34efgh from ELB and put them in ASG standby. stepping through commands now.

oncall-jamie: ```
# remove from target group
aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:us-west-2:...:targetgroup/serving-tg/abcd1234 --targets Id=i-0a12abcd
# set instance to standby in ASG
aws autoscaling enter-standby --instance-ids i-0a12abcd --auto-scaling-group-name serving-asg --should-decrement-desired-capacity
```

incbot: :white_check_mark: ACTION ASSIGNED - oncall-jamie removing affected instances from TGs. severity remains sev2. notify support for customer impact comms.

support-liz: pinged support channels and created triage ticket. affected customers currently seeing elevated latencies and some request failures; added note to status page draft.

pm-alex: recommend partial traffic shift for critical customers only via Route53 weighted records (20% shift to us-west-2a/2b) to reduce exposure while we validate recovery. TTLs are short (60s) should be quick.

eng-runtime-rahul: before shifting traffic, confirm other AZs' capacity for model-serving. check GPU queue lengths.

ops-kelly: other AZs have spare capacity. initiating weighted shift for prod-weighted-records for critical-route.

ops-kelly: ```
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z12345 --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"api.redwood.com","Type":"A","SetIdentifier":"usw2a-weight","Weight":80,"TTL":60,"ResourceRecords":[{"Value":"3.10.20.30"}]}}]}'
# weight updated to route 80% to usw2a/2b, 20% remains for usw2c for canary
```

oncall-jamie: traffic shift in progress. monitoring 5xx rate.

10m later - eng-runtime-rahul: 5xx rate dropped from 6.2% -> 1.1% after removing instances + weight shift. user impact reduced but not fully gone (some errors from legacy edge caches).

incbot: :information_source: AWS Support case opened (case# AWS-987654321) - requested host-level investigation and EBS volume health check.

ops-kelly: AWS replied: observed host NVMe controller firmware issue causing transient io stalls for a subset of instances. host replacement / instance reboot recommended. they will proceed to replace the hypervisor host for i-0a12abcd.

oncall-jamie: scheduling maintenance on the affected instances: terminate & let ASG replace (preferred to avoid volume detach complexity). marking in ASG and letting new instances bootstrap.

oncall-jamie: ```
aws autoscaling terminate-instance-in-auto-scaling-group --instance-id i-0a12abcd --should-decrement-desired-capacity false
# new instance launched, healthy checks passing
```

1h later - sre-lead-ana: new instances finished bootstrap, ELB target group healthy, 5xx rate stabilized at 0.3%. rolling back weighted Route53 to normal (100% usw2c is not safe until we validate; instead we restore even distribution across healthy AZs).

ops-kelly: restored routing to our usual weighted config across AZs; monitoring continues.

pm-alex: external status page updated: "Mitigated - partial traffic shift and instance replacements reduced errors. Ongoing validation with AWS."

support-liz: notified customers via status updates and support channels. only small set of high-throughput tenants saw any dropped requests; no data loss reported.

eng-runtime-rahul: post-incident action items: 1) add an automated healthcheck that detects high avgqu-sz on NVMe and alerts before 5xx spike, 2) document fast-path to remove instances from TGs and auto-failover to other AZs, 3) evaluate pre-warm spare capacity to absorb shifts.

sre-lead-ana: agreed. I'll own the runbook updates and schedule a postmortem with timeline + RCA once AWS provides final host-replacement report.

oncall-jamie: handing off to next oncall at 2419506642 - leaving incident in monitoring state. incident commander transfer to sre-lead-ana.

incbot: :white_check_mark: INCIDENT RESOLVED -> status changed to "monitoring". resolution summary: AWS host-level NVMe controller fault caused EBS IO stalls on subset of instances -> caused ELB 504s due to backend request hang -> mitigated by deregistering affected instances, ASG termination/replacement, and partial Route53 weighted shift. follow-ups assigned.

sre-lead-ana: scheduling postmortem document: https://incidents.redwood.local/postmortems/2419503042-pm

pm-alex: thanks team — great coordination. :thumbsup:

support-liz: closing support ticket after follow-up confirmations from affected customers."
